== Oath Rod and Agelessness ==
I'm not sure that the Oath Rod causes the Aes Sedai agelessness. In New Spring, when Moraine and Siuan swear the oaths, they don't immediately become ageless. Later in the book, Moraine wishes for the ageless face to help her look Aes Sedai. Plus, it's been stated several times that use of the Power causes the agelessness. "You haven't worked with the Power long enough to achieve the agelessness." is said probably more than twenty times throughout the book.

It made have been implied that the oath rod causes the agelessness with the Kin and Damane's lack of ageless faces, and the loss of the agelessness with stilling, but this needs to be stated as an assumption until there is more outright proof (which should come fairly quickly in the last two books).

Anathemys[[Special:Contributions/173.57.82.144|173.57.82.144]] 13:55, April 28, 2010 (UTC)

:Alas Anathemys, I was of the same opinion and was determined to gather as much information as I could find to prove this idea heretical! But I then stumbled across this page here in the wiki: [[Source:Budapest Q&A, April 2003]].  Very close to the bottom of this long report, Robert Jordan makes it quite clear that it is the Three Oaths, taken upon the Oath Rod (or a binder, as it was called in the Age of Legends) that is the source of Aes Sedai agelessness.  I am afraid that you and I aare going to have to swallow our pride and eat our words. [[User:Pedantic|Pedantic]] 23:50, June 19, 2012 (UTC)

== Agelessness Inconsistencies ==
The article addresses one inconsistency, the Rhuidean Aes Sedai appearing ageless but not having shortened lives (and, not mentioned, but living a thousand years before the Oaths were created).  But aren't there others?  At some point, early in the books, doesn't an Aiel mistake an Aes Sedai for a Wise One, and a bit later someone recognizes Wise Ones as resembling an ageless Aes Sedai?  Again, I think this was early, suggesting RJ might not have worked out the Oath Rod's effects early on.  It would also be worth mentioning Egwene's Accepted test, where she saw herself as ageless but revealing she had never held the Oath Rod; although these events were not real, Egwene's Accepted test contained a significant amount  of real, accurate information that Egwene had no way of knowing in reality.  Were there any others agelessness inconsistencies?  --[[User:DavidK93|DavidK93]] ([[User talk:DavidK93|talk]]) 06:18, 21 November 2021 (UTC)

: This is interesting. I always assumed that the agelessness of those Aes Sedai was not "the" ageless look, but something else. It could be a straight up error by Jordan though. The regular ageless look is literally not being able to tell what age the woman is. The ancient AS has a description of fragile skin which no Third Age AS is described as having. We could speculate for reasons why this may be so, maybe the AS was bound with one Oath and we don't know what effect that has, but it would just be speculation. 

:Not sure about Egwene's Accepted test on what can be true or not. If it's a little like TAR (and we know it is related because of the resonance in that scene later), then it could be that what she believes is true and she doesn't know the ageless look is related to the Oath Rod at that point. The Wise One thing rings a bell, perhaps it is in TGH where Verin meets Uriel? I don't think it is as specific as the ageless look, maybe just "you look like you are in charge". I'll check and come back to you. I will ask in the Discord group too. [[User:Moridin 2000|Moridin_2000]] ([[User talk:Moridin 2000|talk]]) 00:18, 24 November 2021 (UTC)

==Lifespan halving questions==
Noticed this on the [[Three Oaths]] article:
:Recently it was discovered that use of the Oath Rod was actually reducing the Aes Sedai lifespans by half

This article seems to reflect that:
:She was offered the choice of being bound and not using the power in such a way (and so to see '''her remaining lifespan halved''')

I guess my question  is - do we have the exact text which relates to this? I'm seeing paraphrasing but would very much like to know the letter of it...
: She has also openly discussed the possibility of releasing Aes Sedai from the oaths upon retiring, letting them live out their full lifespans in peace and joining the Kin.
:Romanda Cassin vehemently opposed this idea, despite being close to the end of her life expectancy.

It's a factor I don't remember in the books but seems like a huge cultural factor. Also given that there are THREE oaths it bears the question of how much lifespan you lose per oath... If three oaths reduce "remaining" lifespan (not total?) but 50% then does one oath reduce it by 16.6ish or is it more of a one-tim thing where any use of the rod is a 50% reduction and subsequent oaths don't reduce it further?

This is an important consideration for those who make more than three oaths. Far as I know this would include Moiraine (who took a 4th oath to obey Siuan) and all members of the Black Ajah (they use the Oath Rod to make 3 new oaths to the Dark One... SIX total) so it'd be interesting to know if doing this reduced their lifespan expectations or not.

If indeed releasing someone from their oath restores the lost lifespan as theorized though, the Black Ajah being released from their original 3 oaths I guess wouldn't actually lose lifespan since they are just replacing the old 3 with the new 3. Only Moiraine in theory might've been reduced another 33% via her 4th oath?

The White Tower Oath rod also got used to "re-swear" the oaths but I don't know how that works like if it would double-count in terms of lifespan reduction. [[User:Tycio|Tycio]] ([[User talk:Tycio|talk]]) 15:54, 21 April 2025 (UTC)

: Hmm, so half is more like an approximation. Most Aes Sedai in the White Tower would be expected to live between 370 (extremely weak) and 680 (Moiraine's strength) years. The mean Aes Sedai life expectancy is around 645 years and median is 620 years. From the last two, "half" is about right, but for people like Daigian, it wouldn't be as much as half - 81% to be exact. For Romanda and others, it's 44%, and it would be typical for them to ignore the significantly weaker Aes Sedai in their mental process. The numbers, I'm afraid, will come from work I've done not yet on the wiki and I'll update soon. I also don't believe the Oath Rod causes Aes Sedai to age faster, but rather puts a limit, so unswearing would restore their expected lifespan in full. The main reason for this is that, if it caused a faster rate of aging, we would see a larger disparity in life expectancy and aging for Aes Sedai of very differing strength. For example, weaker sisters would start to go gray a lot quicker, which they don't appear to. [[User:Moridin 2000|Moridin_2000]] ([[User talk:Moridin 2000|talk]]) 09:51, 1 May 2025 (UTC)
